title: NNPS hosts Take Your Legislator to School Day at Denbigh High - North Tidewater News
text:
Newport News Public Schools (NNPS) hosted state legislators, aides, and local leaders for Take Your Legislator to School Day on December 2 at Denbigh High School. The event aimed to highlight urgent funding needs, particularly for aging school facilities.
According to a press release by NNPS, attendees toured classrooms and the Aviation Academy magnet program. NNPS Chief Operations Officer Rusty Fairheart noted that major renovation projects are planned for Warwick and Denbigh high schools, along with upgrades at several other campuses.
State legislators and local leaders present included Delegate Shelly Simonds, Delegate-Elect Dr. Mark Downey, aides to Downey, Simonds, and Congressman Bobby Scott. Also in attendance were School Board Chair Dr. Terri Best, board member Lisa Surles-Law, NNPS Superintendent Dr. Michele Mitchell, Denbigh Principal Dr. Adria Strothers, and members of the Newport News Education Foundation. Strothers welcomed guests while Best expressed appreciation for community and legislative support for public education.
During the visit, NNPS legislative liaison Patrick Finneran outlined the division’s priorities for the upcoming General Assembly session. Legislators Simonds and Downey discussed bills likely to impact school funding. Superintendent Mitchell emphasized that the session presents a strong opportunity to make lasting improvements. Best highlighted the importance of modern learning environments for student productivity, health, and achievement.
NNPS serves approximately 26,000 students across 40 schools including early childhood centers, elementary, middle, high schools, and combination schools. The district employs roughly 3,900 teachers, administrators, and support staff focusing on preparing students to graduate college-, career-, and citizen-ready. NNPS provides early learning programs as well as advanced science labs and educational technology to support success among students and teachers alike.
